lines.trans: Good thing our partners are not home right now.
My sex hero is in here!
Senya, where are you?
Except Senya stayed behind on room service.
Wait, you were supposed to work it.
Yes, well, he asked me to swap shifts with him.
And what do we do now?
Mikhail, a one-to-one score humiliates us both.
Let me just beat you already and be done with this.
Back off from me, Vitya.
There will be no rematch.
If you want to slap cards around, go play solitaire.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ожитель'). Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'of roommates / partners' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть сожитель.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always of roommates.
The chef immediately noticed where the of roommates was.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'at home', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The main thing is, you keep him at home.

examples.text: А Осипенко сейчас дома лежит. У него больное сердце.
examples.trans: And Osipenko is lying at home right now. He has a sick heart.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will be'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'екс-герой'). Common masculine noun meaning 'sex hero' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть секс-герой.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always sex hero.
The chef immediately noticed where the sex hero was.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'where', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'only', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'room service' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть рум-сервис.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always room service.
The chef immediately noticed where the room service was.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'remained', paired with 'оставаться'.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'but, after all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must').

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to work', paired with 'поработать'.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'просить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'asked', paired with 'просить'.

examples.trans: I wanted to ask you something.
Arkash, I wanted to ask you something.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'меняться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to swap / trade places', paired with 'меняться'.

examples.trans: What for? We swapped, it's mine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'account' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Или счёт в банке. Потому что они все обманщики.
examples.trans: Or a bank account. Because they are all cheats.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'нижать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'humiliates', paired with 'унизить'.

examples.text: Она просто унижает меня перед детьми!
examples.trans: She is simply humiliating me in front of the children!

examples.text: Ты зачем так сильно унижал её?
examples.trans: Why did you humiliate her so much?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'us', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'both', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You both leave here right now.
Get over here right now, quickly, both of you!

examples.text: Вы сейчас отсюда оба уходите. И больше сюда не возвращаетесь. Ясно?
examples.trans: You both leave here right now. And you never come back here again. Clear?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'let's', paired with 'дать'.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ой, кажется, у вас сломан нос!
examples.trans: Oh, it looks like your nose is broken!

examples.text: Завтра у меня важное собеседование на работу.
examples.trans: Tomorrow I have an important job interview.

examples.text: Значит, у нас с тобой много общего.
examples.trans: So you and I have a lot in common.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'играть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'I will win', paired with 'выигрывать'.

examples.text: Паша, эти выборы ты не выиграешь.
examples.trans: Pasha, you won't win this election.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'кончить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'we will finish / be done'.

related.gloss: not to we will finish (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и покончить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and we will finish on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют покончить.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to we will finish.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'валить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'back off'.

examples.text: Отвали, или я сломаю тебе нос!
examples.trans: Back off, or I will break your nose!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'no, none whatsoever', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I have no money at all.

examples.text: Да нет у тебя никаких денег.
examples.trans: But you don't have any money.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'rematch' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть реванш.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always rematch.
The chef immediately noticed where the rematch was.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'with cards' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мне пятнадцать тысяч на карту переведут.
examples.trans: They'll transfer fifteen thousand to my card.
I will pay by bank card.

examples.text: Нет, лучше я это в новости отправлю. Мне пятнадцать тысяч на карту переведут.
examples.trans: No, I'd rather send this to the news. They'll transfer fifteen thousand to my card.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'шлёпать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to slap / flip'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и пошлёпать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to slap on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют пошлёпать.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to to slap.

meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'ложить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'lay out'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и разложить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and lay out on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют разложить.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to lay out.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'solitaire games' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть пасьянс.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always solitaire games.
The chef immediately noticed where the solitaire games was.
